claims.text: A uniform distribution of multiple principal elements promotes formation of a continuous, multi-component oxide film.
The oxide film formed on the high-entropy alloy is self-healing.
The multi-component oxide film mitigates mechanical wear.
The multi-component oxide film mitigates corrosive attack.
The proposed high-entropy alloys possess a uniform nanocrystalline microstructure.
The proposed high-entropy alloys contain equiatomic or near-equiatomic proportions of their principal elements.
Mechanical wear disrupts the passive oxide layer.
Disruption of the passive oxide layer exposes the underlying high-entropy alloy matrix.
High-entropy alloys have high diffusivity along grain boundaries.
Uniform elemental distribution and grain-boundary diffusivity cause rapid re-oxidation at wear-damage sites.
Rapid re-oxidation re-establishes a protective surface film.
The re-established protective film inhibits further mechanical degradation.
The re-established protective film inhibits localized corrosion.
Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the high-entropy alloy will have lower wear volume than the matched conventional-alloy baseline.
Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the high-entropy alloy will have lower corrosion current density than the matched conventional-alloy baseline.
Conventional alloys with similar elemental makeup but lower configurational entropy typically form less uniform or less self-healing oxide films.
The proposed protective mechanism should operate in oxidizing environments that permit oxide-film formation and reformation.
The proposed protective mechanism may fail in highly reducing environments.
The proposed protective mechanism may fail at temperatures that hinder oxide-formation kinetics.
Direct evidence connecting uniform elemental distribution to self-healing oxide formation during simultaneous wear and corrosion is limited.
